policy: Single stars that survived a historical supernova and stand at the centre of its remnant in the nebula overlay. Each star is placed at its own Gaia DR3 distance, which also places its remnant, and every physical value comes from an analysis made at that distance.

stars.name: IRAS 00500+6713
stars.distance_note: 2297 +122/−114 pc: geometric distance from the Gaia DR3 parallax, Bailer-Jones et al. 2021, https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2021AJ....161..147B
stars.temperature_note: the illustrated non-LTE wind model of Lykou et al. 2023 at 2.3 kpc; their best fit spans 200,000–280,000 K
stars.luminosity_note: 36,000 L_sun from the same model; their best fit spans 30,000–60,000 L_sun
stars.note: Central star of the supernova remnant Pa 30, probably the merged remains of two white dwarfs that survived SN 1181. Its wind blows at about 15,000–16,000 km/s. Spectral type WO1 (Gvaramadze et al. 2019, https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.00012) is recorded here rather than in the spectral type field, which reads only Morgan–Keenan and white-dwarf classes. The model radius and the luminosity of Gvaramadze et al. 2019 assume the Gaia DR2 distance of 3.07 kpc and are not adopted; the radius of Lykou et al. 2023 refers to a deeper layer than their temperature, so it is not adopted either. No mass is adopted: Lykou et al. 2023 give a range of 1.0–1.65 M_sun.
